hero.heading:
Effective structures,
by design —
hero.subtitle: You leave with structural decisions that enforce themselves across your systems, software, and workflows. They keep working regardless of which individuals are on the team, which technology you've adopted, or how much discipline a given day allows.
whycurfee.body.1: Complexity grows whenever organisations use discipline as a substitute for structure.
whycurfee.body.2: Targeted structures cannot be designed without understanding what already exists. The work begins with the current reality: what is in place today, and how it behaves under pressure.
whycurfee.body.3: Most structures grow organically because no one has the complete overview, and no one was ever given the ownership to design them deliberately. This applies equally to systems, software, and workflows. The more people, AI tools, and integrations interact, the faster complexity compounds.
whycurfee.body.4: Only those who understand the existing circumstances can make decisions that the structure itself enforces, independent of individual discipline.
whycurfee.body.5: That is the task: to make reality visible, reduce it to its essentials, and embed decisions so that deliberate structures take shape and simplicity sustains itself. The result is an organisation that invests its time and money in value-creating work. The structure carries what discipline and the tireless efforts of individuals used to carry.
observations.heading.status_quo: Does any of this sound familiar?
observations.1.title: Discipline Dependency
observations.1.reality: Conventions and norms only survive as long as someone is watching.
observations.2.title: Structural Fragility
observations.2.reality: Dependencies and connections have grown beyond what anyone fully understands.
observations.3.title: Decisions Without Effect
observations.3.reality: Decisions were documented on paper or in wikis, but nowhere were they consistently enforced.
observations.4.title: Knowledge Concentration
observations.4.reality: Knowledge lives in the minds of individuals and disappears when they leave.
observations.5.title: Workarounds as the Norm
observations.5.reality: What started as an exception is now the norm. No one remembers the original decision anymore.
observations.6.title: Onboarding Friction
observations.6.reality: New employees need weeks or months to find their way around the existing structures.
observations.7.title: AI-Assisted Development
observations.7.reality: AI-generated code reaches the system landscape faster than the structure can integrate it.

approach.diagnosis.1.title: Root cause, every time
approach.diagnosis.1.body: Symptoms get traced to their root cause, one by one. The report names the cause and clears away the noise. You stop fixing what isn't broken.
approach.diagnosis.2.title: Reality over relief
approach.diagnosis.2.body: The diagnosis names reality, even when no one in the room wants to hear it. Recommendations only work if they describe what's actually there, beyond what's been agreed on paper.
approach.diagnosis.3.title: Max. five pages, ready to act on
approach.diagnosis.3.body: A report of no more than five pages, naming the situation, the root cause, and the next decision worth making. It is short enough to act on and clear enough to defend in front of your board.
approach.guidance.1.title: Embedded where the work happens
approach.guidance.1.body: Every agreed solution is embedded where the structure enforces it: a pipeline, a workflow, an approval gate, a schema, a permission boundary, or a routing decision. The structure carries it from there.
approach.guidance.2.title: One change at a time, until complete
approach.guidance.2.body: No change starts until the previous one is integrated into the structure. A change is either complete or pending.
approach.guidance.3.title: Your team implements. I guide each step.
approach.guidance.3.body: Implementation happens inside your organisation, carried by the people who know your environment best. I make sure the design works in practice and the change is integrated into the structure before the next one begins.
approach.sparring.1.title: Complete system context in every conversation
approach.sparring.1.body: In the first month, I get to know your environment: systems, software, and workflows. Every response is grounded in your specific circumstances.
approach.sparring.2.title: Honesty, even if it takes time
approach.sparring.2.body: If a decision offers short-term solutions with long-term consequences, I address this openly with you. Structural integrity is a priority. Short-term speed is secondary.
approach.sparring.3.title: A predictable rhythm
approach.sparring.3.body: Sparring takes place in fixed, scheduled sessions. Decisions are reviewed again in one of these sessions. The process is predictable on both sides.
fields.diagnosis.heading: Where root causes usually hide.
fields.guidance.heading: Where discipline overrules structure.
fields.sparring.heading: Where decisions need pressure-testing.
fields.diagnosis.1.title: A landscape no one designed.
fields.diagnosis.1.body: Tools were added incrementally, each chosen to solve a specific problem. None was selected as part of a coherent whole. Data is fragmented across multiple systems. Integrations depend on the individuals who built them.
fields.diagnosis.2.title: Architecture no one chose.
fields.diagnosis.2.body: The architecture grew through incremental decisions, never as a single design. Years of changes accumulated. Dependencies multiplied. The original intentions have been lost over time.
fields.diagnosis.3.title: Coordination doing the work of structure.
fields.diagnosis.3.body: Approvals are routed via email. Roles overlap. Decisions are delayed. Individuals carry the coordination that the structure should carry.
fields.diagnosis.4.title: Between the layers.
fields.diagnosis.4.body: Some root causes cannot be attributed to a single domain. They arise at the intersection of systems, software, and workflows. The symptoms often appear far from the root cause.
fields.guidance.1.title: Conventions that exist only through discipline.
fields.guidance.1.body: The convention was agreed in a meeting. Months later, inconsistencies have multiplied across teams, services, and processes.
fields.guidance.2.title: Boundaries enforced only by individual memory.
fields.guidance.2.body: Boundaries between teams, services, and systems exist only by convention; the structure carries none of them. New hires identify them only by crossing them. Each crossing comes at a cost the team pays.
fields.guidance.3.title: Exceptions that have become the norm.
fields.guidance.3.body: What began as a one-time exception is now the default. No one remembers the original decision.
fields.guidance.4.title: Judgement trapped in individuals.
fields.guidance.4.body: The same recurring decisions end up on the same managers, engineers, and team leaders' desks week after week. Each time, the same judgement produces the same answer. The structure carries nothing forward.
fields.sparring.1.title: Decision bottleneck at the desk
fields.sparring.1.body: Every structural decision across your systems, software, or workflows always ends up on the same one or two desks.
fields.sparring.2.title: High-stake commitments
fields.sparring.2.body: You are about to commit to a multi-quarter technical strategy: a re-architecture, a platform migration, vendor lock-in, or a new platform operating model. The last comparable decision took far longer than planned.
fields.sparring.3.title: Compounding small decisions
fields.sparring.3.body: A decision in one place forces dozens of workflows into rework. A new policy in one department subtly alters an entirely different process. The cost only becomes visible months later.
fields.sparring.4.title: Technical realignment after a major change
fields.sparring.4.body: An acquisition, a major hire, a new product line, or a regulatory change has reshaped your environment. The technical decisions that fit yesterday no longer fit today.
about.heading: Philipp Höllinger
about.who.location: From Salzburg · across the DACH region
about.background.heading: Where my approach comes from
about.principles.heading: How I work
about.principles.1.text: Symptoms reveal the direction. Root causes demand resolution. The work begins where the chain ends.
about.principles.2.text: A standard that depends on individual discipline is not sustainable. The structure must enforce it.
about.principles.3.text: Workarounds lead to a structure that no one chose. Lay a solid foundation, and you can build anything upon it.
about.credentials.1.title: Roots in Logistics
about.credentials.1.body: I started by coordinating workflows between goods, employees, and processes. The lesson that stayed: when people with different approaches have to work together, structure matters more than discipline.
about.credentials.2.title: From Computer Science to Architecture
about.credentials.2.body: After my studies, I moved into software engineering and then to architecture. Architecture was the logical next step. I've always wanted to keep both the big picture and the details in mind, because one is incomplete without the other.
about.credentials.3.title: Addition by Subtraction
about.credentials.3.body: Most system landscapes I encounter suffer from bloat: too many tools, too many discipline-based standards and conventions, and inflated workflows and processes. Improvements usually come from reduction. Doing less is harder than doing more, and that's precisely where the real gain lies.
about.credentials.4.title: The Lesson behind Decision Enforcement
about.credentials.4.body: I repeatedly saw decisions documented in detail and ignored in practice. People remembered the convention until focus moved elsewhere. The lesson: structure must enforce what discipline alone cannot sustain.
about.credentials.5.title: Continuous Improvement
about.credentials.5.body: Every project taught me the same lesson: a deliberate decision pays off in the long term; a shortcut compounds in cost until it is addressed. This asymmetry is why I address structure from the start, before complexity compounds against you.
about.credentials.6.title: Structure in the Age of AI
about.credentials.6.body: In the age of AI, structure is more important than ever. AI only sees what fits into its context, with no awareness of frameworks, guidelines, or boundaries. The system has to enforce these, and that only works if the underlying structure is reliable.
quote.text: Doing less is harder than doing more. That's exactly where the real gain lies.
calltoaction.heading: Just have a question?
calltoaction.subtitle: Send a quick note. I'll reply within 2 to 3 working days.
differentiator.1.title: Think structurally.
differentiator.1.body: Structure is leverage. Each embedded decision becomes a compounding improvement that pays off many times. The work done once does not need to be done again.
differentiator.2.title: Reality before recommendation.
differentiator.2.body: Recommendations only work when they describe what's actually there, beyond what's been agreed on paper. You get the honest version, even when no one in the room wants to hear it. Reality is the only solid foundation.
differentiator.3.title: Self-sustaining by design.
differentiator.3.body: Every engagement ends with you owning the result. Your team carries the implementation. When the engagement is done, the structure carries on without me.
engagements.heading: Selected engagements
engagements.1.title: Booking platform, rebuilt around integrity
engagements.1.situation: A booking system enabled the very errors it was meant to prevent. Courtrooms were double-booked, past-dated bookings went through, and conflicts went unchecked.
engagements.1.issue: Transactional integrity, validation rules, and database constraints were missing from the booking system.
engagements.1.built: The system was rebuilt to enforce data integrity at every layer, refusing any booking that conflicted with another or fell outside the rules of a valid booking.
engagements.1.outcome: Duplicate bookings disappeared. Hearings stayed on schedule and rescheduling costs vanished.
engagements.2.title: Regional events, redesigned around self-service
engagements.2.situation: For several years, five students, one per region, spent each summer reading emails sent by event organisers and entering every event into the system by hand.
engagements.2.issue: Each region collected event data its own way, in unstructured emails and inconsistent formats.
engagements.2.built: A self-service form let event organisers submit their own listings. An automated import loaded the submissions into the system daily, and an approval mechanism replaced the manual review the students used to do.
engagements.2.outcome: What used to be a summer job became a single click.
engagements.3.title: Publishing system, built around SDG compliance
engagements.3.situation: The EU Single Digital Gateway required administrative information to be available in a structured, multilingual, and machine-readable format, crawlable for EU infrastructure.
engagements.3.issue: No publishing system existed that could produce content in a structured, multilingual, machine-readable format.
engagements.3.built: A publishing system was built from the ground up, designed around predefined form fields that editors filled out to create or update entries. Metadata tagging, publication, and a structured translation workflow for German and English content were handled automatically in the background.
engagements.3.outcome: Editors kept filling fields. Anyone in the EU needing Austrian administrative information could find it in two languages.
about.who.role: Structural Architect for systems, software, and workflows
about.curfee.c.text: Familiarise myself with what exists today.
about.curfee.r.text: Make sense of the insights gained.
about.curfee.e1.text: Eliminate everything that does not matter.
about.curfee.e2.text: Embed the remaining elements so the decisions enforce themselves.
about.why.heading: Why I do this
about.who.hero.1: I'm not interested in the next big hype. My goal is to reduce complexity by designing deliberate structures with forward-looking decisions, structures in which the decisions, once embedded, enforce themselves and prepare for what comes next.
about.who.hero.2: Structures evolve organically over time, and that is the norm. The most common mistake I have seen is implementing systems, software, and workflows before their impact is fully understood: before anyone knows how each element affects the organisation and its employees, and before anyone has a complete picture of the environment.
about.who.quote: What drives me is an obsession with the things that go unnoticed, the small details that shape the future of an environment.
about.who.why.3: Leaders and teams need an overview and concrete guidance. They need an honest picture of the current state, of formal and informal communication, of tool usage, and of workflow handover.
about.who.why.1: Most conversations about structural change revolve around the same terms: transformation, modernisation, agility, and readiness for the next trend. But these words rarely move things forward.
about.who.why.2: I am a minimalist and an advocate of simple concepts. Deliberate structures are the benchmark for efficiency and the foundation for adapting to whatever comes next.
about.who.why.4: This is Curfee's approach: structure over discipline, solid foundations from the start, embedded decisions over written policy, and the willingness to address uncomfortable truths.
about.who.hero.3: That's why I start with what already exists before streamlining workflows, tools, or processes.

meta.home.description: Curfee is a structural architecture practice for systems, software, and workflows, run by Philipp Höllinger in Salzburg, Austria. Architecture decisions are embedded in pipelines and tooling so the system itself enforces them, regardless of individual discipline. Three engagements for technical decision-makers across the DACH region: Diagnosis, Guidance, and Sparring.
meta.home.jsonld.description: Curfee is a one-person structural architecture practice based in Salzburg, Austria, founded in 2026 by Philipp Höllinger. It serves CTOs, engineering managers, team leads, and founders across Austria, Germany, and Switzerland (DACH region) with three engagements across systems, software, and workflows: Diagnosis (root cause analysis from 2 weeks), Guidance (implementation from 3 months), and Sparring (ongoing retainer). The work applies the Decision Enforcement Principle: architecture decisions are enforced by the system itself through pipelines, automated checks, and tool configuration, regardless of individual discipline, memory, or vigilance.

schema.decision.enforcement.name: Decision Enforcement Principle
schema.decision.enforcement.description: The Decision Enforcement Principle is an architecture approach in which decisions are enforced by the system itself, through pipelines, automated checks, and tool configuration, regardless of individual discipline, memory, or vigilance. Developed and applied by Philipp Höllinger at Curfee across systems, software, and workflows, the principle treats a decision as embedded only when the structure carries it forward without human intervention. It is the core principle behind every Curfee engagement.
